$comment: The landing lemniscate: which concepts sit on the thread, and where (#52).
ADR-0003 asks for a committed layout rather than a force simulation, so the figure is
byte-identical across builds and a node's position is a decision someone made rather than
an accident of a solver. Before this file, the landing page picked `allNodes.filter(tier)
.slice(0, 3)` — alphabetically first — while a comment above it claimed the layout was
already committed. The right lobe read Adam / AdamW / ALiBi.
POSITION IS `t`, NOT x/y. Each node names a fraction along its lobe, and the renderer
resolves it through `pointAt` in src/lib/curve.ts — the same function that draws the
stroke. Raw coordinates would let a bead drift off the path the moment the curve was
nudged; a `t` cannot. The decision stays committed, the geometry stays derived.
HOW A NODE EARNS A PLACE. The left lobe is gold and holds verified concepts; the right is
teal and holds frontier ones. That is the figure's whole argument — reviewed core flowing
into new growth — so tier decides the lobe and nothing else may.
Within a lobe the bar is RECOGNITION, not centrality. This page has ten seconds to get a
stranger onto a node, so a name someone arriving cold already half-knows is worth more
than the node with the most edges. `causal-masking` outranks `attention` on connectivity
and would be a worse invitation.
Three beads per lobe, because the handoff staggers the frontier pulse over three delays.
Labels go on the beads at t=0.2 and t=0.8 and never the one at t=0.5: mid-lobe is the
figure's widest point, and the stroke runs straight through the text there. That is four
labels, which is what the handoff asks for and as many as a 620px figure holds.
Every id here is checked against /content/nodes by `validate:content`, which also rejects a
bead whose tier belongs to the other lobe, a t outside 0-1, and a duplicate.

Written when the left lobe was every verified concept there is. It no longer is — 27 of 57 are verified as of the Optimization batch — so the lobes are now a CHOICE among many rather than a listing, and recognition is the whole of the bar. A bead also cannot simply stay: verifying a node moves it off the teal lobe by force, because validate:content rejects a bead whose tier belongs to the other one. That is how backpropagation left this file, and it is the mechanism that will keep bringing someone back here.
this file is where someone decides whether it displaces one.
